articles.title: External Users
articles.content:
# External Users

## Purpose

The **External Users** section in ViciECM allows administrators to manage existing external user access by updating the expiry time and controlling the access level.

## Features

- **View External Username:** Displays the existing external username. This field is read-only and cannot be modified.
- **Update Expiry Time:** Allows administrators to modify the expiry date and time. This is a mandatory field.
- **Control Access Level:** Allows administrators to set the access level to **Read** or **Edit**.
- **View External User Details:** Displays information such as the username, access mode, logical path, job name, workflow name, and expiry time.
- **Edit External User Settings:** Allows administrators to modify the available settings using the Edit (pencil) icon corresponding to an existing entry.

## How to Update an External User

1. Navigate to **Administration → External Users**.
2. Locate the external user whose settings need to be updated.
3. Click the **Edit (pencil) icon** in the corresponding row.
4. View the **External Username**. The username cannot be edited.
5. Select the required **Access** level: Read or Edit.
6. Enter or select the required **Expiry Time** using the date and time fields. This field is mandatory.
7. Click **Update** to save the changes.
8. Click **Cancel** to discard the changes.

## Access Levels

- **Read:** Provides read-level access to the shared resource.
- **Edit:** Provides edit-level access to the shared resource.

*The exact permissions associated with each access level depend on the application's configuration.*

## Important Notes

- The external username is displayed for reference and cannot be modified.
- **Expiry Time is mandatory** and must be specified when updating an external user's settings.
- Verify the selected access level and expiry time before saving changes.

articles.title: User Management
articles.content:
# User Management

## List of Functionalities

### Buttons 
- Add User
- Import User
- Swap User
- Inactive User
- Export to PDF / Excel with
  Current Page / All Pages Dropdown

### Actions
- Edit (Click on Edit)
- We will get 4 options - Update - Add to group - Profile Edit - Cancel.

## List of Columns in the Data Grid
- Photo
- Username
- First Name
- Last Name
- Mobile No.
- User Type
- User Pool
- Department
- Email ID
- Status
- Actions

## Add User (Just Click on the Button)

### Username (Mandatory Field)
- Once user is created, it cannot be changed.
- Min 1 Character is necessary.
- Max 50 Characters. 
- Accepts Alphabets, Numbers, and Alphanumeric characters.
- Cannot create Username Duplicates as it is Case - insensitive.

### Password / Change Password
- Once password is created, can be updated again.
- Password and Confirm Password has to match.
- It is Case - Sensitive.
- What kind of characters are accepted and how many characters depends on Pwd Rules Tab in the Configuration.

### First Name
- This is a Mandatory Field.
- Min 1
- Max 100
- All characters allowed except few Special Characters like $%<> , 

### Type of User (Mandatory)
- Administration: This user has much higher access then normal or Scanner user.

- Normal:  Can't access Admin Module
         - Can't access few Portlets in Dashboard Module like All Jobs, Backup Details, Volume Information, User Information, Logged in Users and Data Extraction.

 - Can't access few Sub - Modules in Manage like Purge Mails, Upload Logo, there is no "ALL USERS" Hyperlink in the recycle Bin. And also, no access to metadata import.

- A normal user cannot access Workflow - Designer but if he is added to a group called as 
"WFDESIGNERGROUP" that allows the normal user to access designer menu.

- Workflow - No Form Reports.

- Reports - No ECM.

- Workflow Reports - Normal - Cannot access User wise Job Details
- Workflow-wise job details only available for the Super-Admin.

- Scanner - Only used to Scan and upload the physical documents into the Repository.

- By Default, this type of user has no permission   for Cabinet Creation and Document type Creation.

### User Pool (Mandatory)

- Named User Pool: Licenses are assigned individually to users. To accommodate new users beyond the license limit, existing users must be removed to free up licenses.

- Concurrent User Pool: Total licenses = 25; total users = 50. Only 25 users can access the repository at a time on a first-come, first-served basis.

### Email ID (Mandatory)

### Cabinet Creation
- User cannot create new Cabinets without this permission.

### User cannot create new Doc Type without this permission.

### User Status
- Set to Active / Inactive.

### Add to group  
- Can add new / existing user / inactive user to any single / Multiple groups.

## Inactive User
- Using this, you can turn active users into Inactive users.
- You can turn single / multiple users into inactive users.

## Swap User
- Using this feature, We can transfer the ownership of the files from old user to new user.
- In this process, User Type will also get swapped.
- The New User will replace old user
- The files and folders the new user will have = new user + old user
- On the other hand, The old user becomes inactive.

## Export
- The Export dropdown provides two options for exporting the user list:
   1) Current Page: Exports the user list displayed on the current page.
   2) All Pages: Exports the complete user list across all pages.
- The user list can be exported in Excel or PDF format.

## Import Users
- Using this feature, we can download a sample Excel template (.xlsx) and upload a list of multiple users to create them in a single operation.
- We should ensure that all mandatory fields in the Excel sheet are populated. Non-mandatory fields can be left blank.
- We should not delete any existing columns from the Excel template, as doing so may cause the Import Users process to fail.

articles.title: Basics of Deployment
articles.content:
# Manual Deployment Process

## 1. Basics

### 1.1 What is Deployment?
- Applying changes to an existing application using Patch / Build Files is called Deployment.

### 1.2 What is Services Application?
- It is an application that displays a list of all the programs that actually run in the background.
- Press `Win + R` and type `services.msc` to open the Services window.

### 1.3 What is a Patch?
- A targeted fix of a bug can be called a Patch.

### 1.4 What is a Server and a Client?
- A computer providing services to other computers is called a Server.
- It receives requests from clients, processes those requests, and sends back a response.
- The Client's request is usually sent to the Application Server, which requests the necessary data from the Database Server.
- The Database Server sends the data to the Application Server, and the Application Server sends the data back to the Client.
- When accessing Google Chrome, the browser can act as a Client.
- An application requesting services from a server is called a Client.

### 1.5 What is an Environment?
- A setup where an application is installed and running for a particular purpose, with a particular version of the application.

#### Types of Environments
- DEV → Development
- QA → Testing
- UAT → User Acceptance
- PROD → Live / Production Use

---

## 2. Deployment Process

### 2.1 Stop the Required Services
- Press `Win + R`.
- Type `services.msc`.
- Stop the following services:
  - Text Extraction
  - Format Converter
  - Doc Manager
  - Workflow Escalation

### 2.2 Download the Patch Files
- In the Support Repository, the team will create a job with the required files attached.
- Log in as the assigned user and download the attached files.

### 2.3 Prepare the Deployment Folder
- Press `Win + R`.
- Enter the shared path.
- Run the batch file, which creates the required folder structure with the current date.
- Log in to the Support Repository.
- Navigate to `Workflow → My Jobs → Process → Attachments`.
- Download the necessary files.
- Move or paste the files into their respective folders.

### 2.4 Execute the Patch
- Run the Patch.
- Select Incremental Backup.
- This automatically creates a folder with the current date.
- The Full Backup option takes too much time.

### 2.5 Update Deployment Documentation
- Update the Bugs List file.
- Rename the Excel file using the assignee's name.

### 2.6 Restart Services and Verify the Application
- Once the patch work is completed, start the services again.
- Try logging in to the application.

### 2.7 Rollback Procedure
- If you are unable to log in to the application, you can use the rollback script with the Team Lead's permission.

---

## 3. Server Details

### 3.1 Deployment Server
- Server: VTPL-079
- Shared Path: `\\vtplsvr03\f\InternalRelease\ViciCloud 9.1.1.9`

articles.title: Manual Deployment Process
articles.content:
# VTPL-079 - Application Patch Deployment Procedure

## 1. Pre-Deployment Preparation

### 1.1 Locate the Update Files
- Navigate to the local PC's root directory where the application update files are provided.
- Navigate to the specified network path where the deployment-related files are stored.

### 1.2 Verify and Update Flags.ini
- Locate the `Server` folder and open `Flags.ini` using Notepad++.
- Before modifying the file, open Windows Registry Editor (`regedit`) and verify the existing application version number.
- Identify and note down the following:
  - Current Version Number: The version currently deployed.
  - Next Version Number: The version to which the application will be upgraded.
- Update the required version details in `Flags.ini` based on the registry information and deployment requirements.

## 2. Target Server and Patch Preparation

### 2.1 Access the Target Server
- Select the target server: `VTPL-079`.
- Access the VTPL-079 server.

### 2.2 Collect the Required Patch
- Locate and collect the required application patch file from the provided update location.
- Navigate to the directory containing the `Database` folder.
- Copy and paste the required application patch file into the same directory where the `Database` folder is located.

## 3. Create the Deployment Folder

### 3.1 Create a Date-Wise Folder
- On the local PC, navigate to:

C:\Vici-Updates\


- Create a new folder using the current deployment date.

Example:

C:\Vici-Updates\30-10-2026\

### 3.2 Copy the Database Folder
- Copy and paste the required `Database` folder into the newly created deployment folder.
- Verify that all required database scripts and deployment-related files are available before proceeding.

## 4. Stop IIS and Application Services

### 4.1 Stop IIS
- Open Command Prompt with Administrator privileges.
- Execute the following command:

cmd >iisreset -stop

### 4.2 Stop Application Services
- Stop the required application services on VTPL-079.
- If any service does not stop normally, identify the corresponding process through:

Task Manager > Details`

- Terminate the relevant process if required and authorized.

## 5. Backup and Patch Extraction

### 5.1 Execute the Deployment Package
- Execute the required patch deployment package.
- The deployment process will automatically initiate a backup.

### 5.2 Perform Incremental Backup
- Select the `Incremental Backup` option, if prompted.
- Verify that the backup process completes successfully.

### 5.3 Extract the Patch
- Once the backup is completed, allow the patch extraction process to continue.
- Ensure that the extraction process completes successfully.

## 6. Database Script Execution

### 6.1 Open SQL Server Management Studio
- Copy the extracted database scripts.
- Open SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS).

### 6.2 Execute Repository-Level Scripts
- Select the `VICIECMSS` database (Repository level).
- Open the SQL Query Editor.
- Copy and paste the required database scripts one after another.
- After pasting each script, click `Execute` to run it.
- Follow the prescribed execution order.

### 6.3 Execute RP-Level Scripts
- Select the `RpDOCmgr` database (RP level).
- Open the SQL Query Editor.
- Copy and paste the required database scripts one after another.
- After pasting each script, click `Execute` to run it.
- Follow the prescribed execution order.

### 6.4 Verify Script Execution
- Verify that each script executes successfully without errors.
- Proceed to the next script only after checking the execution result.
- Ensure that all required database scripts have been executed.

## 7. DCOM File Execution

### 7.1 Locate the DCOM File
- Locate the DCOM file provided with the deployment package.

### 7.2 Execute the DCOM File
- Execute the DCOM file as required by the deployment instructions.
- Verify that the execution completes successfully.

## 8. Application Configuration Changes

### 8.1 Review Configuration Instructions
- Review the `.txt` files provided with the patch.
- Identify the configuration changes specified in the respective text files.

### 8.2 Apply Configuration Changes
- Apply the required changes to the corresponding application configuration files and locations.
- Verify that the configuration values have been updated correctly.

## 9. Restart Application Services and IIS

### 9.1 Start Application Services
- Start all the required application services on VTPL-079.
- Verify that the services are running successfully.

### 9.2 Start IIS
- Open Command Prompt with Administrator privileges.
- Execute the following command:

cmd > iisreset -start

### 9.3 Verify IIS Status
- Confirm that IIS has started successfully.
- Ensure that all required application services are running.

## 10. Post-Deployment Verification

### 10.1 Application Verification
- Access the application and verify that it loads successfully.
- Confirm that the updated application version is reflected correctly.

### 10.2 Database Connectivity Verification
- Verify application connectivity with the database.
- Ensure that there are no database connectivity errors.

### 10.3 Functional Verification
- Perform basic application functionality checks.
- Verify that the application modules are accessible and functioning as expected.

### 10.4 Deployment Completion
- Confirm that all deployment activities have been completed successfully.
- Report any issues encountered during deployment to the concerned team.
